scenarios.title: Training: navigation and picking
scenarios.question: Training (about 4 min). Pan, orbit and zoom; hover a cell to see its values; click to select it; press C on two cells to compare them. Say aloud what you see. No answer needed.
scenarios.questionVr: Training (about 4 min). Walk around the table; point the right controller at a cell to see its values; pull the trigger to select it; press A on two cells to compare them. Look at your left wrist to open the menu. Say aloud what you see. No answer needed.

scenarios.title: Turnout by voting district
scenarios.question: Which voting district has the LOWEST turnout?

scenarios.title: Income vs turnout
scenarios.question: Column height = estimated mean income, colour = turnout. Do the lowest-income districts have lower or higher turnout than the rest?

scenarios.title: Income vs Sweden Democrats
scenarios.question: Column height = estimated mean income, colour = SD vote share. Where is the SD share highest?

scenarios.title: DeSO: median income and country of birth
scenarios.question: DeSO areas: height = median income, colour = share born abroad. How do the two relate?
options: Higher income where more residents are born abroad
Higher income where fewer residents are born abroad
scenarios.expected: Higher income where fewer residents are born abroad

scenarios.title: Four variables at once
scenarios.question: Grid columns: up = population density, down = share aged 65+, colour = mean income; buildings = turnout of their voting district. Find the tallest columns (densest cells). Which description fits them best?
options: Low income, few residents 65+, low-turnout district
High income, many residents 65+, high-turnout district
Low income, many residents 65+, high-turnout district
High income, few residents 65+, low-turnout district
scenarios.expected: Low income, few residents 65+, low-turnout district

scenarios.title: Children and older residents (optional)
scenarios.question: Grid columns: up = share of children 0-15, down = share aged 65+. Look at the tall columns (many children): how deep do they go below the ground?
options: Shallow: where children are many, older residents are few
Deep: children and older residents live in the same places
scenarios.expected: Shallow: where children are many, older residents are few
